chunks: And with the first chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja‘far, peace be upon him, who said:
When Amirul Mu'minin, peace be upon him, was in Kufa, after he led the people in the last evening prayer (Isha), he would call out to the people three times until the people of the mosque could hear:

"O people! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy upon you, for the call of departure has been made among you. So what is the meaning of clinging to this world after the call of departure has been made in it?! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy upon you, and move on with the best provision you have with you, and that is Taqwa. And know that your path leads to the Resurrection, and your passage is over the Sirat, and the greatest horror is before you. And on your path there is a steep pass difficult to climb, and terrifying, fearful stations that you must inevitably pass through and halt at.

Then it is either the mercy of Allah — exalted is His majesty — and thus salvation from its terror, the greatness of its danger, the harshness of its appearance, and the severity of its reality; or else it is perdition, after which there is no recovery."

key_terms.التعرج: Clinging or lingering — refers to attachment to worldly life
key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa — consciousness of God, piety, guarding oneself from sin
key_terms.الصراط: The Sirat — the bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.المعاد: The Place of Return — the Resurrection and final reckoning
key_terms.انجبار: Recovery or restoration — the impossibility of remedy after perdition
key_terms.عقبة كؤود: A steep, difficult mountain pass — metaphor for the trials of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about preparing for death and the afterlife in his sermon after Isha prayer in Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam Ali's (AS) practice of delivering a powerful admonition to the people of Kufa after the Isha prayer, calling them three times to prepare for death and the Hereafter. He urged them to take Taqwa (God-consciousness) as their provision, warning them of the terrifying stations on the path to Resurrection and the Sirat Bridge, emphasizing that one's outcome is either divine mercy leading to salvation or perdition with no recovery.
